Method settings

Intergreen 0 reproduces the workbook exactly. Enter the real amber + all-red to share only the green, since ARTS Max Green excludes intergreen.

What each setting means
  • Start-up (3 s): lost time when the green starts, while the first drivers react and pull away.
  • Headway (2.1 s/veh): green each queued vehicle needs to cross the stop line.
  • Factor (1.5): safety margin; the green needed = (start-up + headway × vehicles per cycle) × factor.
  • Sat. flow (1,800 veh/h/lane): most a lane can pass in an hour of green; used for DS = volume ÷ (sat. flow × green ÷ CL).
  • Default lanes per detector: lanes the critical LS counts for when a stage row leaves Lanes blank.
  • Intergreen / stage: flashing green + amber + all-red between stages. 0 reproduces the op-sheet; the real value (e.g. 10 s) shares only the green, as ARTS Max Green excludes intergreen.
  • Min / Max CL: the range the proposed cycle is kept within (it is rounded up to 5 s).
  • Flow gap min / max: flow gap = existing green ÷ vehicles per cycle (s/veh). Below the min the green is too short to clear the queue; above the max it is more than the traffic needs (the stage may run empty, or the gap setting may cut it early).
  • Approach on a grade: Yes when the critical approach climbs towards the stop line. Vehicles move off more slowly uphill, so a flow gap up to 7 s/veh is accepted. It changes only this check, not the greens or CL.
  • Method: HCM op-sheet (formula above) or Volume ratio from the weekly count book: total green = (Σ critical + Added to Σ) ÷ veh/h per 1 s green, shared by volume, + Add per stage, rounded to Round to.

Daily profile

List the cluster's junctions in order along the road, with the distance between neighbours (the master's distance is 0 m in Cluster List). The tool estimates Low and High Offsets from travel time minus a queue allowance, then draws a time-space diagram and measures the green-wave bandwidth both ways. Opens with a made-up three-junction cluster (J1, J2, J3) so you can see how it works.

Cluster

Junctions in order along the road, first to last. Use ▲ ▼ to move one, or Reverse order. This order is used everywhere: offsets, the time-space diagram, Simulate and the Live junction corridor.

JunctionGap from previous (m)CSQueue allow. (s)ConfiguredMaster

Order = position along the road. Queue allowance starts that junction's green earlier so a standing queue clears before the platoon arrives.

Load a Cycle Log export from CC (Start, End, Plan Name, Cycle Length, Stage Name, Executed Green, Pedestrian, Degree of Saturation) and see what the junction actually ran in each plan. Map layout (optional)

Quickest way: in Google Maps, frame the junction, copy the link from the address bar, take a screenshot of the map only (Win+Shift+S), press Ctrl+V here, paste the link and click Set scale from link. Keep the browser zoom at 100% and do not resize the picture.

Custom tile address

Needs internet. Street map: CARTO with OpenStreetMap data; satellite: Esri World Imagery (the credit is printed on the map; check each provider's terms for your organisation's use). The scale is set automatically. Road centre lines (blue; purple = one-way) come with it so you can trace by snapping, or create every approach of a junction in one click.

Trace the real junction on an OpenStreetMap map or a Google Maps screenshot (north up, scale bar visible). The 3D view and the Live junction ("From the map layout") follow it: the picture becomes the ground, cars use your approaches, lanes and turning shares. Saved in the project Excel file.

3D view

Cluster in 3D opens the Live junction corridor in 3D (each junction with its own saved setup). Junction in 3D opens the Live junction in 3D: your junction exactly as set up there (type, lanes, slip roads, stages by LS, vehicle mix), on the map layout if you traced one.

Watch a junction vehicle by vehicle and change the timing while it runs. Choose the junction type (4-arm, T-junction or custom), keep your Control Centre diagram beside the setup, and set each approach like the diagram: the movements each lane allows (left, straight, right, U-turn) with its loop, the turning shares, and which movements run in each stage. Vehicles pick a lane that allows their movement, follow the turning path, and right-turners give way to oncoming traffic when both get green. Movements without a signal (a left-turn slip road, the through road of a T-junction) can be set to Give way or Free flow. Below: the signal program, driver behaviour, an evaluation (delay, queues, LOS, Executed Green, compare and export) and a corridor run with the Offsets tab. Choose fixed time or vehicle actuation in Stages. A learning and testing tool with simplified driver behaviour, not certified traffic-engineering results.

    Cycle timeline

    Stage by stage, second by second: queues building and clearing, vehicles crossing the stop line, loop calls. Step back through the last 30 minutes of the run.

    Driver behaviour

    reaction time, aggressiveness, speeds, vehicle classes, saturation flow check

    Evaluation

    Runs the junction as it is set up now, without drawing, and measures every vehicle. Change the timing and run again to compare.

    Validation and queue calibration

    Checks the simulation against the site: volumes (GEH against the LS counts on Tab 1), queues (against the range you see on site) and signals (Executed Green against the cycle log on Actual vs plan). Uses the warm-up, period and runs set under Evaluation.

    Queues seen on site at this hour (longest queue in a normal cycle)

    Run in SUMO / VISSIM

    Take this junction, as set up here (lanes, arrows, control, stages and intergreen, demand from Tab 1, vehicle mix and driver behaviour), into another simulator and bring the results back as a scenario to compare with the Evaluation above. Uses the warm-up, period and runs set under Evaluation.

    SUMO (free, open source)

    Plain SUMO files with run.bat. Install SUMO from eclipse.dev/sumo, unzip, double-click run.bat, then import the run*_tripinfo.xml, run*_queue.xml and run*_detectors.xml it writes.

    VISSIM

    VISSIM cannot run in this tool. The input workbook lists links, inputs, routes, compositions, signal groups and program, detectors and starting values for driving behaviour. Name the links as in the workbook ("A in", "B out"), then export Node results or Movement evaluation as .att and import it here.

    Corridor (green wave)

    Time-space diagram, last 5 minutes: each junction's main-road signal in both directions (upper bar eastbound, lower bar westbound; green / amber / red, grey = no signal, such as a free-flow through road at a T-junction) and the vehicles that entered at either end (blue eastbound, orange westbound). In a green wave the lines pass through the green bars without going flat. Click a junction above to show it in the panels; the junction picture above shows the whole corridor (drag and zoom to look closer).

    Travel time survey

    Uses the Cycle and Offsets choices above. Runs without drawing, then puts the corridor back.

    Build a road network the way VISSIM does it, in fewer steps: put the map underneath, click to place each junction, join the junctions with roads, then let the tool fill in lanes, loops, volumes and signals from each junction's controller configuration and detector counts. Works for a corridor or a grid. Run it to watch the junctions work together.
